approach: The problem still exists: `critic_brief` (`crates/athena-context/src/briefs/planner.rs:185-210`) prints only the plan under review, and `critic_round` builds `CriticInputs` with only the current plan and Athena's findings (`crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs:353-359`). From round 2 on, code now adds a section "Earlier rounds on this plan" before "Plan under review". For each earlier critic round it prints the findings the planner was shown (the stored critique's findings: Athena's and the critic's). Beside each it prints the planner's answer. For a round before the last, the answer is the approach and decisions of the plan that followed it. For the last earlier round, the answer is the plan under review itself, which is not repeated; the brief says so and gives a code-computed list of what changed. That list compares the last reviewed plan with the plan under review, item by item on exact text (approach, each decision, file, step, risk, dependent, demonstration, open question). It prints the changed or new items and the removed items, and says every other part is unchanged since the critic last reviewed it. The history comes from `closing.plans` and `closing.critiques`, which `end_round` fills in step (`planning.rs:483-484`), through a new pure builder `earlier_rounds` in `planning.rs` and a new `EarlierRound { plan, findings }` brief input in the context crate. Nothing is stored and no record type is added. `critic.md` gets two bullets, 403 bytes in total so the frame stays under the 900-token bound at `lib.rs:570`. The first tells the critic to check from round 2 that each earlier blocker or major was resolved. The second tells it to raise a major only on a part the brief lists as changed or new, or on a defect earlier rounds missed that stops the plan working or leaves a criterion unshown, with file:line evidence, and otherwise to report it as minor, 'even where a rule above says major'. That wording settles the clash with the always-major lines (critic.md lines 8, 10, 15). Round 1's brief, the planner brief, the 5-round cap and the any-major-forces-a-round rule are not touched. No refusal or matching rule is added: `plan_changes` only describes differences, so the refusal corpus does not apply.

decisions.choice: Code supplies what changed. A private `plan_changes(previous, current)` in planner.rs (visible to briefs.rs tests as pub(super)) compares the last reviewed plan with the plan under review, one item at a time, using a small `Item` enum that derives PartialEq over the record structs (approach, steps and open questions compared trimmed). The brief prints 'Changed or new: ...', 'Removed: ...' (only when non-empty) and 'Every other part is unchanged since round N-1.', or 'Nothing changed: the plan under review is identical to the round N-1 plan.' Labels are short (Approach; Decision 2: first 60 chars; File path; Step 3: ...; Risk: ...; Dependent name; Demonstration for criterion 4; Open question: ...). Reordered but identical items count as unchanged.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2. The critic is told to limit new majors to changed parts, so the brief must show which parts those are; the critic cannot infer it from findings alone. The comparison is by exact text, so it is code, not model memory (the mechanism default). Only one earlier plan is compared (the last reviewed one), because that is the plan the critic last judged in full. The size stays small: labels, not plan text. The comparison errs toward over-reporting a reworded item as changed, which lets the critic look at it again and never hides a change.

rejected.option: Show every earlier plan in full
rejected.why: Each round would add a whole plan of several KB; the brief grows without bound and the critic still has to diff by eye.

rejected.option: Ask the critic in prose to compare with what it remembers
rejected.why: The critic is a fresh invocation each round and remembers nothing; this is the failure the request describes, and the mechanism default forbids relying on prose.

rejected.option: Compare by position, item by item (step 3 against step 3)
rejected.why: One inserted step would mark every later step as changed. Matching on exact item text ignores position.

rejected.option: Show a line diff of the rendered plan bodies
rejected.why: A line diff needs long context to read and breaks on harmless re-wrapping; labelled items match how the critic's findings cite locations.

decisions.choice: The critic.md rule is narrowed and states which rule wins. Bullet A: 'From round 2, check first that each blocker and major finding under "Earlier rounds" was resolved in the plan under review; name any that was not.' Bullet B: 'From round 2, raise a major only on a part the brief lists as changed or new, or on a defect earlier rounds missed that stops the plan working or leaves a criterion unshown, with file:line evidence; otherwise minor, even where a rule above says major.' Both are added as the last list items, after the 'In round one' line, each on its own line.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 3. Without a bar, any new defect counts as 'missed before'. Bullet B limits the exception to a defect that makes the plan fail or leaves a criterion unshown, requires evidence, and says it wins over the always-major lines 8, 10 and 15 for parts that did not change. Changed or new parts keep every existing rule. The two bullets total 403 bytes, so the frame is 2236+403 = 2639 bytes, about 880 estimated tokens, under the 900 bound at lib.rs:570. Line 16 ('In round one') already scopes an earlier rule by round, so the pattern exists. The wording is pinned by a test, and the remaining risk is stated in D189.

rejected.option: Keep the first draft ('a defect you can show earlier rounds missed' with no bar)
rejected.why: Every new finding is by definition one earlier rounds did not raise, so it would let every new major through.

rejected.option: Edit lines 8, 10 and 15 to add 'except from round 2'
rejected.why: Changes existing wording that other tests pin (lib.rs:640-706, briefs.rs:1741-1769) and costs more bytes than the room under the 900 bound allows.

rejected.option: Forbid any new major from round 2
rejected.why: Hides real defects in changed parts and in the plan's untouched weak spots; criterion 3 keeps both exceptions.

decisions.choice: Answer shape. For each earlier round before the last, print 'Planner's answer (the round k+1 plan):' with its approach and each decision as 'choice Reason: reason' (no rejected options). For the last earlier round, print 'Planner's answer: the plan under review below (round N).' and then the changed list, with no repeat of the plan's approach or decisions.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 6. The latest answer is the plan under review, so repeating it prints the same text twice and blurs which text is under review. Older answers appear nowhere else in the brief, so they are printed. The extra text is bounded: at the 5-round cap there are at most 3 older answers.

rejected.option: Print approach and decisions for the latest round as well
rejected.why: Duplicates the plan body and confuses which copy to review.

rejected.option: Print no older answers, only findings and the changed list
rejected.why: The request asks for the planner's answers; older rounds' replies are not visible anywhere else in the brief.

decisions.choice: History data model: `EarlierRound { plan: JobPlan, findings: Vec<Finding> }` in the context crate, one per earlier round, oldest first. `earlier_rounds(plans, critiques, before_round)` in planning.rs pairs each critique with the plan of the same round in `closing.plans` and skips a critique with no plan. The brief derives each round's answer from the next entry's plan, or from `inputs.plan` for the last.
decisions.reason: `end_round` pushes the reviewed plan and its critique together (planning.rs:483-484), and the stop paths push both (312-313) or the plan alone (350) and then stop, so inside the loop the two lists line up by round. `Closing` is created fresh per run (mod.rs:299-300, 1362) and `plan_round` is called once (mod.rs:1372), so the lists hold only this job's rounds. A mechanical pass returns `RoundEnd::Mechanical` without pushing (planning.rs:251-269), so a plan sent back by Athena's own checks is never a round. Pairing by round number keeps the 'critique k belongs to plan k' rule in one place and leaves the 'answer to round k = plan k+1' rule to the brief builder. No field is added to JobPlan, Critique or PlanOutput (criterion 4).

rejected.option: Add an `answers` field to PlanOutput and JobPlan
rejected.why: Changes the planner's output schema and prompt (out of scope), every plan fixture and a `deny_unknown_fields` record (records/plan.rs:95-97); the plan text already holds the answer.

rejected.option: Read the critique files back from the records branch
rejected.why: Records are written only at close, so the in-memory Closing is the only same-run source; a file read adds failure paths.

decisions.choice: Prove 'identical to today's output' with a recorded digest. Before editing `critic_brief`, add `critic_brief_without_earlier_rounds_is_todays_brief`: it takes `critic_brief(&critic_inputs())`, cuts it from '## History file' to the end, hashes that tail with `athena_data::sha256_hex`, and asserts the digest equals a literal recorded from the unmodified code. It also asserts the brief has no '## Earlier rounds' and equals the with-history brief after the section is cut out.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 5. The old critic tests check substrings only (briefs.rs:2859-2961), so a stray change outside the section would pass. The tail from '## History file' holds everything the change can touch (the insertion point, plan body, Athena's findings, soundness, critique) and only fixed text and the `plan(1)` fixture. The head (title, request, reading, system facts) is left out on purpose: it embeds the live `defaults.toml` through `AcceptedReading::new(&reading(), &defaults(), ..)` (briefs.rs:1604-1606) and `SYSTEM_FACTS` (briefs.rs:1500), which this change itself edits, so a digest of the head would break on unrelated edits. The cut-equality check covers the head.

rejected.why: It embeds docs/system-facts.md, whose critic budget line this change edits, and the live defaults.toml.

rejected.why: Puts a second copy of the logic under test in the test; the recorded digest is the data.

risks.risk: A critic told to treat unchanged parts leniently may miss a real defect in them.
risks.mitigation: Bullet B limits a new major on an unchanged part to a defect that stops the plan working or leaves a criterion unshown, shown with file:line evidence, and says that rule wins over the always-major lines. Changed and new parts keep every rule. D189 and the changelog state the limit; whether a model critic follows the bullets, and how many 5-round stops this prevents, is not measured.

risks.risk: A planner that rewords an untouched item without changing it makes that item look changed, so the critic may raise a major on it.
risks.mitigation: The comparison is by exact text, trimmed, and ignores order, so it errs toward listing a reworded item as changed, which lets the critic look at it again and never hides a change. The comparison is a unit test (`critic_brief_plan_changes_compare_items_by_exact_text`).

risks.risk: critic.md has only about 20 estimated tokens of room under the 900-token frame bound at lib.rs:570, and the facts line could be forgotten.
risks.mitigation: The two bullets are given verbatim (403 bytes) and total 880 estimated tokens against the 900 bound. The frame-size test and the budgets test fail loudly if the producer lengthens them, and the producer sets the facts line from the budgets test's failure message.

risks.risk: The critic brief grows each round, which adds cost to later critic calls.
risks.mitigation: At the 5-round cap the brief holds at most 4 rounds of findings, 3 older answers (approach and decision text, no rejected options) and one label list. This is an estimate of a few KB, not measured. The caps are per invocation and do not read brief size (planning.rs:347).

risks.risk: The recorded digest in `critic_brief_without_earlier_rounds_is_todays_brief` breaks when another job edits the critic brief's fixed text.
risks.mitigation: The digest is of fixed text and the `plan(1)` fixture only. The failure message prints the new digest; a legitimate edit of the critic brief's fixed text (soundness text, no-change rule) updates the literal in the same change. The head is covered by the cut-equality check instead of the digest.

risks.risk: The first critic round of a resumed job has no history (its seed comes from an earlier job, mod.rs:1366-1370).
risks.mitigation: The limit is stated in the changelog and D189. The seed's findings still reach the planner as before; round 1's brief stays unchanged, as the accepted reading says. The test for the resumed path is the existing `a_retry_of_a_job_stopped_in_planning_carries_the_last_critiques_findings` (job_plan.rs:1042), which reads the reader brief only.

risks.risk: docs/system-facts.md is not in the reading's deliverable list, so a scope check could flag it.
risks.mitigation: The edit is one number, forced by budgets.rs:125; the file is not governance (admission.rs:36-41, 63-68) and is a planned file in this plan, so the verifier does not count it as unplanned (plan.rs:177-180).

demonstrations.method: Add `the_second_critic_brief_carries_round_ones_findings_and_the_planners_answer` to crates/athena-cli/tests/job_plan.rs. It builds `Fixture::with_config(&planned_config())` and a `Scenario` with two plans and two critiques. Plan 1 is `good_plan()`. Plan 2 is `good_plan()` with approach 'ANSWER-MARK add the greeting line and its test.' and steps ['Edit README.md.', 'STEP-MARK add the greeting test.']. Critique 1 is `critique_of("revise", &[("major", FINDING)], None)`; critique 2 is `critique_of("accept", &[], None)`. The script is `scenario.script()` wrapped in a closure that pushes each `Role::Critic` `user_prompt` into a shared Vec (the wrapper pattern at job_plan.rs:1054-1061). The test calls `athena.ask` and `athena.go` and asserts the job lands. Critic brief 0 holds neither FINDING nor 'Earlier rounds on this plan'. Critic brief 1 holds '## Earlier rounds on this plan', '### Round 1: findings', FINDING with its '[major] (critic) at demonstrations' prefix, 'Planner's answer: the plan under review below (round 2).', the exact line 'Changed or new: Approach; Step 2: STEP-MARK add the greeting test.', and 'Every other part is unchanged since round 1.' It holds 'ANSWER-MARK' exactly once (in the plan body, not repeated in the history) and does not hold the round-1 plan's approach text 'Add a greeting line to README.md.' in the history section.
demonstrations.observes: Two critic prompts are captured through the real planning path (`Athena::go` -> `plan_round` -> `critic_round`). The first has no history. The second has round 1's finding, the planner's answer (the plan under review plus the code-computed change list), and no duplicate of the answer text.
demonstrations.fails_without: Before the change the round-2 critic brief has no 'Earlier rounds on this plan' section, no round-1 finding text, no 'Planner's answer' line and no changed-items line, so the first assertion on critic brief 1 fails. The test compiles on the old code (it uses only public API).
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: `Athena::go`, which reaches `plan_round` and `critic_round` in crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs. Guards: planning enabled by `planned_config()` (`[job_plan] enabled = true`); both plans pass Athena's own plan rules like the existing `good_plan()`, so no mechanical pass intervenes. Fixture: `Fixture::with_config` and `Scenario` in crates/athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs (exists; Scenario.plans and .critiques feed the fake planner and critic at common/mod.rs:690-721). Injection: a wrapper closure around `scenario.script()` passed to `fx.athena(..)`, as at job_plan.rs:1054-1061 (exists). The fake only returns scripted JSON; the brief text under test is built by the real `critic_brief` and `earlier_rounds`. The new test is added by step 7.

demonstrations.method: In crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs tests, next to the critic tests at line 2859, add three tests. (1) `critic_brief_without_earlier_rounds_is_todays_brief`, written first and run on the unmodified `critic_brief` to record the digest: it cuts `critic_brief(&critic_inputs())` from '## History file' to the end, hashes it with `athena_data::sha256_hex` and compares with the recorded literal; it asserts no '## Earlier rounds'; and it asserts the brief equals the with-history brief after the text from '## Earlier rounds' up to '## Plan under review' is removed. (2) `critic_brief_lists_earlier_findings_the_planners_answers_and_what_changed`: two `EarlierRound`s built from `plan(1)` and `plan(2)` with the existing `finding(..)` helper, and a plan under review `plan(3)` that differs from `plan(2)` by a new approach marker, a second step and a removed risk. It asserts: the section sits after '## History file' and before '## Plan under review'; '### Round 1: findings' comes before '### Round 2: findings'; each finding's severity, source, location, summary and evidence are present; round 1's answer prints plan 2's approach marker and 'CHOICE-MARK ... Reason: REASON-MARK' but not 'REJECTED-MARK' (checked inside the history section only); round 2's answer is 'Planner's answer: the plan under review below (round 3).' with the exact lines 'Changed or new: Approach; Step 2: STEP-MARK second', 'Removed: Risk: RISK-MARK drift' and 'Every other part is unchanged since round 2.'; and the lower-cased brief holds none of 'cost', 'usd', '$' (as at briefs.rs:2887-2897). (3) `critic_brief_plan_changes_compare_items_by_exact_text`: identical plans give 'Nothing changed: the plan under review is identical to the round 2 plan.'; reordered steps are unchanged; a changed decision reason marks 'Decision 1: ...'; trailing whitespace on the approach is unchanged; a removed dependent is listed under Removed.
demonstrations.observes: The section is present only with history, holds the findings and answers in round order with the right fields, the change list is exact, there are no banned words, and with no history the brief is byte-for-byte today's.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the new field and section the tests do not compile, or the history assertions fail. A stray change outside the section fails the tail digest. A section printed with an empty list fails the 'no ## Earlier rounds' assertion.

demonstrations.method: Add the test to crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs with `repo_with_planning(3)` and `run_planned`. Planner queue: [`bad_plan()`, A, B, C], plans built from `good_plan()` with distinct approach markers 'ANSWER-A', 'ANSWER-B', 'ANSWER-C'; B and C have steps ['Edit README.md.', 'STEP-B add the greeting test.'] and A has the one default step. `planning_script` repeats only the last queue entry (tests.rs:1333-1335), so the four planner calls are: `bad_plan` (sent back mechanically in round 1, never filed: planning.rs:251-269), then A (round 1 critic), B (round 2 critic), C (round 3 critic). Critic queue: [`revising_critique()` with summary F1, `revising_critique()` with summary F2, `accepting_critique()`]. The job lands. Read `prompts_of(&calls, Role::Critic)`. Critic 0 (reviews A): no 'Earlier rounds on this plan', no F1. Critic 1 (reviews B): '### Round 1: findings' and F1; the line 'Planner's answer: the plan under review below (round 2).'; the exact line 'Changed or new: Approach; Step 2: STEP-B add the greeting test.'; 'ANSWER-B' exactly once (plan body); 'ANSWER-A' not at all; no F2; no 'ANSWER-C'. Critic 2 (reviews C): '### Round 1: findings' with F1 before '### Round 2: findings' with F2, exactly two '### Round' headings; round 1's answer 'Planner's answer (the round 2 plan):' holds 'ANSWER-B' (once); round 2's answer says the plan under review below (round 3); the exact line 'Changed or new: Approach' (no Step in the list); 'ANSWER-C' exactly once; 'ANSWER-A' not at all. Then `git diff --stat` shows no path under crates/athena-data, and planning.rs reads only `closing.plans` and `closing.critiques`.
demonstrations.observes: The critic's history grows round by round from this job's own filed plans and critiques only. Critique k is paired with the plan it reviewed, the answer to round k is the next round's plan, and the planner's own mechanical revision is not a round.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the `earlier_rounds` builder the round-2 and round-3 critic prompts carry no history and the first history assertion fails. A builder that filed Athena's mechanical pass as a round would give 3 round headings in critic 2, not 2.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: `Athena::go` through `plan_round` and `critic_round` (planning.rs:30 and 318). Guards: `repo_with_planning(3)` turns planning on with max_rounds 3 (tests.rs:294-299); round 3 is the last round, and an accepting critique ends planning cleanly. Fixture and injection: `run_planned(repo, planner_queue, critic_queue)` (tests.rs:1350) builds `planning_script` (tests.rs:1316), which feeds scripted JSON to the fake driver and records every prompt in `Calls`; `prompts_of` (tests.rs:1420) reads them. All exist. Only the test is added (step 7). The brief text is built by the real `critic_brief` and `earlier_rounds`; the fake returns scripted JSON and does not build the history.

demonstrations.seam: The recorded checks themselves (`fmt`, `clippy`, `test`), run by Athena and the verifier as cargo commands; no seam is needed.

demonstrations.method: Read `git diff CHANGELOG.md docs/decisions.md docs/system-facts.md`. CHANGELOG.md gains one bullet under [Unreleased] / ### Changed in the file's style: root cause (job 20261115-202532-6mng, 5 rounds, $14.32, the 37 earlier jobs), the fix with file and function names, the limits (whether a model critic follows the new bullets and how many 5-round stops it prevents are not measured; a resumed job's first round has no history) and the test names. docs/decisions.md gains `## D189 · ...` appended after D188 with Case, Decision, Alternatives, Tradeoff (including the remaining risk that the critic can still raise majors on changed parts, and that the unchanged-part bar rests on the critic's judgment), Reversal cost and a Provenance bullet; no earlier line changes; it avoids 'amends', 'supersedes' and 'superseded by'. docs/system-facts.md changes only the critic budget line. `git diff --stat` lists only the files in this plan; no athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflow or records/ path appears. Then run `cargo test -p athena-core mirrors`, `cargo test -p athena-data decision_links`, `cargo test -p athena-cli --test backtest` and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test mirrors`.
demonstrations.observes: An appended D189 with a Provenance bullet, one changelog bullet, one changed number in the facts file, no governance, workflow or records change, and the log guards pass.
demonstrations.fails_without: A decision inserted inside an earlier entry, one without a Provenance bullet, or one using a link phrase fails the DecisionEntries or AppendOnly rule or the link tests. A missing changelog bullet shows in the diff.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points: the `DecisionEntries` and `AppendOnly` rules (crates/athena-core/src/mirrors.rs:121 and 139), `link_problems` through `decision_gate` (crates/athena-core/src/run/checks.rs), `decision_links` (crates/athena-data/src/decision_links.rs), and the backtest and mirrors tests in crates/athena-cli/tests. All exist. `is_governance` (admission.rs:63-68) is false for each changed doc path.
